_note: Sources for Form 2 Geography (Batches G2-1 and G2-2, Terms 1 and 2). Computed answers use the formulae named here; figures are rounded and must be checked.

world-population.ref: UN World Population Prospects (world population milestones: 1 billion about 1800 … 8 billion on 15 November 2022); geography textbooks on population distribution and its factors
world-population.supports: The growth milestones, factors of rapid growth, effects on resources, density = population ÷ area, densely and sparsely populated regions and the factors.
world-population.checked: Milestones from general knowledge, not opened in this session: please check.

demographic-indices.ref: Crude birth rate, crude death rate and rate of natural increase (per thousand)
demographic-indices.supports: BR = births ÷ population × 1000; DR likewise; NI = BR − DR; ‰ ÷ 10 = %.
demographic-indices.checked: Standard formulae; values computed by code.

equatorial-zone.ref: The equatorial climate and the exploitation of the equatorial forest (as in Cameroonian Form 2 geography)
equatorial-zone.supports: Location, climate (26–27 °C, range 2–3 °C, over 1500–2000 mm of rain), vegetation, resources, methods of exploitation, problems and solutions.
equatorial-zone.checked: Standard textbook content; figures are typical values: please check.

cameroon-regions.ref: Areas of Cameroon's ten regions (km²) and rounded population estimates; deforestation in Cameroon; protected areas Dja, Lobéké, Korup
cameroon-regions.supports: The density practical (areas: Adamawa 63 701, Centre 68 953, East 109 002, Far North 34 263, Littoral 20 248, North 66 090, North-West 17 300, South 47 191, South-West 25 410, West 13 892; populations in thousands are rounded estimates for practice) and the further study on deforestation.
cameroon-regions.checked: From general knowledge, not opened in this session. The population estimates in particular must be checked against the latest BUCREP/INS figures.

tropical-zone.ref: The tropical (savanna) zone and the exploitation of its resources; the firewood crisis (as in Cameroonian Form 2 geography)
tropical-zone.supports: Location (about 5°–15° N and S), climate (25–30 °C, 500–1500 mm, wet and dry seasons, harmattan), vegetation, resources, herding, ranching (SODEPA), cotton (SODECOTON), irrigated rice (SEMRY at Yagoua and Maga), problems and solutions (Green Sahel operation); causes, signs, consequences and solutions of the firewood crisis.
tropical-zone.checked: Standard textbook content and general knowledge, not opened in this session: please check the figures and company names.

biological-resources.ref: Non-timber forest products of Cameroon and the biological resources of its zones
biological-resources.supports: Eru (Gnetum), njangsa, bush mango (Irvingia), bitter cola, kola, Pygeum (Prunus africana), rattan, raffia, honey, shea, gum arabic; methods of collection, importance and sustainable harvesting; resources of the forest, highland, savanna and coastal zones; protected areas Dja, Lobéké, Korup, Waza, Bénoué.

hot-desert.ref: The hot desert milieu and water scarcity
hot-desert.supports: Location (about 15°–30°), climate (over 40 °C by day, cold nights, under 250 mm), daily range = highest − lowest (computed), resources, the Tuareg, oases; causes, signs, consequences and solutions of water scarcity; household water = people × litres × days (computed).
hot-desert.checked: Standard values; arithmetic computed by the engine.

rural-africa.ref: Countrysides in Africa: agricultural landscapes, rural settlement patterns, attractive and repulsive aspects, rural exodus
rural-africa.supports: Forest, highland and savanna landscapes; dispersed, nucleated and linear settlements; push and pull factors; solutions to rural exodus.
